England in the last century, which has been more especially cited as an example of this
form of government, was in point of fact an essentially aristocratic state, although it

struggle which was going on between the nobles and the people without considering the probable
issue of the contest, which was in reality the important point. When a community really
has a mixed government, that is to say, when it is equally divided between two adverse principles,
it must either pass through a revolution or fall into complete dissolution.
